content: The test image shows a corn ear with a large black, sooty/powdery mass replacing the kernels — classic smut morphology. The husk is pulled back revealing a dark black spore mass covering the entire ear. This points strongly to either Common Smut or Head Smut.

The reference Common Smut image shows a smaller black gall on the stalk. The test image shows the entire ear converted to a large black spore mass — this is consistent with severe Common Smut on the ear (Ustilago maydis), which produces large, dark galls that rupture to release black powdery teliospores. The scale and location (ear, not tassel) distinguishes this from Head Smut, which typically replaces the tassel/head structure.
